caveats: The match is at the published spot coordinates, 50-320 m from Oneiric's own Connecting Ridge point, which sits in a local dip and scores 63.78% at 2 m over the same window. Never quote the published 88-92% figures as Oneiric's own Connecting Ridge result.
No coordinate-matched published figure exists for any other Oneiric site; the remaining 32 sites are validated only by the shared method.

Oneiric's shackleton-rim point is 0.00% sunlit at 0 m and 2 m over 18 years (local hollow); whether the hollow is real or the coordinate mis-placed is unresolved. Do not claim validation at Shackleton rim.
command: npx tsx illumination-check.ts --site glaser-spot-N --height 2|10 --series-start 2023-01-01 --series-days 6575 --step 10 (driver in evidence/illumination-check/illumination-check.ts; spot skylines built by pipeline/build-skylines.ts from the published coordinates)
driverValidation: Reproduces the height-report number exactly: Connecting Ridge, 2 m, 6.5-day sortie from 2027-03-01: meanDisc 36.78%, dark gap 23.17 h. Step sensitivity (10 vs 30 vs 60 min) <= 0.05 pts on every definition.

source.method: Horizon method, 20 m LOLA DTM, Sun as disc, 0.5 deg azimuth steps, 1 h steps; window stated as 19 years (abstract) and 20 years (results/figures), no dates given.
source.window: Engine window 2023-01-01 + 6575 d (18.0 years), 10-min steps, 946800 samples per spot.

summary: The engine matches published LOLA-based illumination figures at the sub-1-point level at the four Glaser et al. (EPSC 2014) Connecting Ridge spots: mean visible solar-disc fraction within 0.15-0.62 points, time with any sunlight within 0.29-0.65 points, longest dark within 0.04-0.22 days, longest light within 0.04-0.44 days. All differences sit well inside the published inter-tool spread (~3 pts) and the nodal-cycle annual spread (1.6-2.4 pts). Small one-sided bias (engine 0.15-0.65 pts below published); cause not isolated.
